articles.headline: PhRMA Sues Over Trump Policy Mandating Lower Drug Prices in Medicare
articles.summary: PhRMA has filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration's GLOBE pilot program, which ties Medicare reimbursement for certain drugs to international reference prices from peer countries — potentially reducing prices by 50-80% for affected drugs. The industry argues the program constitutes unlawful price controls dressed up as a voluntary model, while the administration contends it introduces market-based competition. The legal outcome will determine whether international reference pricing becomes a durable structural feature of Medicare drug payment.
articles.why_it_matters: If the courts uphold the GLOBE model, it establishes a legal precedent enabling broad international reference pricing across Medicare, compressing margins for large-cap pharma and biopharma names with significant Medicare revenue exposure.

articles.headline: The Thin Margin of Safety in Selling Compute
articles.summary: MBI Deep Dives dissects CoreWeave's economics as a 'spread business' — raising debt, buying Nvidia GPUs, and renting them out — unpacking why EBITDA is misleading (depreciation is 54% of revenue) and why EBIT multiples also flatter capital-intensive compute sellers. The piece builds a bottoms-up MW-based model to estimate what return on capital CoreWeave needs to justify its current stock price, concluding that the margin of safety for equity holders is thin as demand-supply dynamics in compute eventually normalize. It uses this framework to assess the broader risk of commoditization for pure-play compute sellers as hyperscaler supply comes online.
articles.why_it_matters: Provides a rigorous, practitioner-grade valuation framework for AI infrastructure equity — directly actionable for investors weighing whether to own CoreWeave or other compute sellers as the current demand-supply imbalance in GPUs narrows.
